title: Pediatric Frontal Sinus Obliteration with Bioactive Glass S53P4
content: Frontal sinus obliteration is a procedure usually reserved for select cases of refractory chronic rhinosinusitis, tumors and trauma management. These conditions are relatively rare in children, which makes the procedure even rarer in the pediatric population. Bioactive glass S53P4 is a biocompatible mineral allogenic material used in various applications in maxillofacial, orthopedic and head and neck surgery. Although its’ osteo-stimulating and antibacterial properties, as well as clinical outcomes are well documented in literature, limited data exists about its’ use in frontal sinus obliteration in children is scarce. We present two cases of successful frontal sinus obliteration with S53P4 in different clinical indications, where an inflammatory process and an osteoma have produced bone destruction between the frontal sinus, the orbit and the anterior crania fossa. Bioactive glass in both cases has proven to be easy to use and effective in achieving frontal sinus obliteration in a pediatric patient.
